requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was initially absent, then created and directly observed as appworker with UID/GID 1000. It remained present with its home directory after restart.

requirements.requirement: Set appworker login sessions to a limit of 8,192 open files and 256 processes.
requirements.summary: A persistent PAM limits policy sets both soft and hard nofile to 8192 and nproc to 256. Direct PAM-backed appworker login sessions reported those exact effective limits before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, connection loss bounded the disruption, a different boot ID was observed afterward, and system health, account state, policy, home accessibility, and effective limits recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear roles: creating the required account (cmd-676255a913fa4301), installing its limits policy (cmd-77ab37b015e04940), and performing the mandatory evidence reboot (cmd-fec5a6eb376d4cc8). No unnecessary mutation was identified. After restart, the system was running with no failed units, package health remained sound, and exposed sockets were unchanged apart from expected process-ID turnover.
